[MR-CC-POL-004 §1] 1 Purpose and scope

Customer Care Remedy & Goodwill Policy
Meridian Roasters Co. Document reference: MR-CC-POL-004 Version: 4.0 Effective: 1
November 2025 Supersedes: v3.1 (effective 14 March 2024) Owner: Director of Customer
Experience Review cycle: annual, or on material change to the remedy ladder Approval: CX
Leadership Group, 22 October 2025

This policy governs every financial or material remedy offered to a Meridian Roasters
customer, across both the direct-to-consumer and wholesale channels. It defines who may
authorise what, under which conditions, and to what value.
It applies to:
• Goodwill credits and account credits
• Full and partial refunds
• Replacement product despatched at no charge
• Subscription extensions and free cycles
• Wholesale credit notes and invoice adjustments
• Relationship recovery packages under §7.4
It does not govern statutory refund obligations, which are handled under MR-LEG-POL-002
and always take precedence over anything written here. Where a customer has a statutory
right to a remedy, that right is honoured in full regardless of the caps in this document, and
the difference is booked to the statutory remedy cost centre rather than to goodwill.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §2] 2 Principles

Four principles govern every decision made under this policy.
Proportionality. The remedy should be proportionate to the harm, not to the volume of the
complaint. A calm customer who has suffered a genuine product failure is owed more than
a loud customer who has suffered an inconvenience.
Attribution honesty. The remedy band depends on who caused the problem. Where the
fault lies inside Meridian, the customer should not be worse off than if the fault had lain
with a carrier. §7.3 exists because that was not always true under v3.1.
Single touch. A customer should receive one remedy decision, not an escalating sequence
of small offers. Agents are expected to determine the correct remedy once and offer it in
full. Incremental bidding damages trust more than a slightly low first offer.
Documented rationale. Every remedy above the Tier 1 threshold requires a written
rationale recorded against the case. "Customer was unhappy" is not a rationale. The
rationale must name the fault, the attribution and the clause applied.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §3.1] 3.1 Direct-to-consumer loyalty tiers

| Tier | Qualification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze | Default on account creation | Includes all trial and one-off purchasers |
| Silver | Six completed orders, or an active subscription running twelve weeks | Tier is evaluated nightly |
| Gold | Eighteen completed orders, or an active subscription running fifty-two weeks, or trailing twelve-month spend above USD 600 | Tier is sticky for ninety days after qualification lapses |

Tier is a property of the customer record and must be read from the customer profile at the time of the decision. It must not be inferred from order volume in the conversation, because sticky-tier customers will look under-qualified.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §3.2] 3.2 Wholesale account tiers

| Tier | Qualification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trial | First ninety days from onboarding | No standing remedy authority; every case goes to the account manager |
| Standard | Post-trial, annual contract value below USD 40,000 | |
| Flagship | Annual contract value at or above USD 40,000, or designated by the Commercial Director irrespective of value | Designation is reviewed annually and may be held for strategic reasons |

Flagship designation is not purely numerical. Accounts may be designated flagship because they are reference customers, because they occupy a strategic city, or because they influence a wider buying group. The designation is recorded on the account record and is authoritative.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §4] 4 The standard remedy ladder

Remedies escalate through four steps. An agent should identify the correct step and offer it directly rather than climbing the ladder in conversation.

Step 1 — Acknowledgement and explanation. No financial value. Appropriate where the customer experienced a minor delay within the tolerance published on the order
confirmation, or where the complaint concerns a matter of taste preference rather than
product defect.
Step 2 — Replacement. Replacement product despatched at no charge, on the next
available despatch. Appropriate for a single defective bag, a wrong item shipped, or a grind
error. Replacement is preferred over credit wherever the customer's underlying want is
coffee rather than money.
Step 3 — Partial credit. A credit against the order value, typically between twenty-five and
fifty per cent. Appropriate where the customer received usable product that fell short of
specification, or where a delay materially reduced the value of the product without
destroying it.
Step 4 — Full refund plus goodwill. Full order value returned, plus a goodwill credit
toward a future order. Appropriate where the product was unusable, where a service failure
was repeated, or where the attribution sits squarely inside Meridian.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §5] 5 Goodwill credit caps

The following caps apply to the goodwill component only. They are the maximum a remedy
may reach before any uplift under §7 is applied.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §5.1] 5.1 Direct-to-consumer

| Tier | Standard cap (USD) |
|---|---|
| Bronze | 25 |
| Silver | 50 |
| Gold | 120 |

[MR-CC-POL-004 §5.2] 5.2 Wholesale

| Tier | Standard cap (USD) |
|---|---|
| Trial | 100 |
| Standard | 250 |
| Flagship | 500 |

[MR-CC-POL-004 §5.3] 5.3 Reading the caps correctly

The cap is a ceiling, not a target. Most cases resolve well below it. An agent that offers the
cap by default is not applying judgement and will be picked up in case review.
The cap applies per incident, not per contact. A customer who opens three tickets about the same defective delivery is one incident. A customer who has a delivery failure in January and a quality failure in March is two incidents and two caps.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §6] 6 Approval matrix

| Remedy value (USD) | Authority required |
| :----------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Up to 150          | Customer care agent, acting alone                                                 |
| 151 to 500         | Customer care supervisor                                                          |
| 501 to 1,250       | Director of Customer Experience, or CX supervisor with written Finance concurrence |
| Above 1,250        | Director of Customer Experience and Finance Director, jointly                     |

The 150 threshold is absolute. No role, system, automation or agent may issue a remedy above USD 150 without a named human approver recorded against the case. This applies irrespective of customer tier, irrespective of how obviously justified the remedy is, and irrespective of whether the value sits inside the tier cap. A gold-tier customer owed the full 120 cap is within an agent's authority; the same customer owed 160 under an uplift is not.
Automated systems that propose remedies must record them in a proposed state and must not represent a proposal to the customer as a decision.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7] 7 Conditions and exceptions

This section did not exist in v3.1 and is the substantive change in v4.0. Under v3.1, remedy value was determined solely by customer tier. Post-incident review through 2024 and 2025 found this produced perverse outcomes: a customer harmed by a Meridian production failure received the same ceiling as a customer inconvenienced by a carrier, despite the two cases differing entirely in attribution and in relationship damage.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7.1] 7.1 Attribution categories

Every remedy decision must first assign one of four attribution categories.
Customer-attributable. Incorrect address, refused delivery, storage or brewing error, change of mind. No remedy beyond Step 1 is owed, although discretionary Step 2 remains available for relationship reasons.
Third-party-attributable. Carrier delay, carrier damage, weather event, port closure, public-holiday cut-off, or any failure originating outside Meridian's control. Standard caps in §5 apply unchanged.
Company-attributable. Any failure originating inside Meridian, including production
error, quality-control failure, blend specification deviation, mis-pick, roasting fault,
inventory error, or a procurement failure that propagated into the product. Uplift under §7.3
applies.
Mixed or undetermined. Where two independent causes affected the same customer, or
where attribution cannot be established on the evidence available. Treated as company-
attributable for remedy purposes, on the principle that the customer should not bear the
cost of our uncertainty. The case must be flagged for root-cause review.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7.2] 7.2 Attribution is evidence-based

Attribution must be supported by evidence from the operational record, not inferred from
the customer's description. A customer reporting that coffee "tasted stale" has not
established attribution; the batch record, the lot record and the quality note have.
Where a complaint concerns product quality, attribution requires tracing the affected order
line back to its roast batch and green lot. Where a complaint concerns delivery, attribution
requires the shipment exception record and, where a weather or holiday cause is claimed,
external corroboration.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7.3] 7.3 Company-attributable root cause uplift

Where attribution is company-attributable or mixed, the applicable goodwill cap rises by
one band:

| Channel | Standard band | Uplifted band |
| :-------------- | :------------ | :------------ |
| D2C bronze | 25 | 50 |
| D2C silver | 50 | 120 |
| D2C gold | 120 | 250 |
| Wholesale trial | 100 | 250 |
| Wholesale standard | 250 | 500 |
| Wholesale flagship | 500 | 1,250 |

The uplift does not change the approval matrix in §6. A gold customer uplifted to 250 still
requires supervisor approval above 150.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7.4] 7.4 Relationship Recovery Allowance

For flagship wholesale accounts where all of the following hold:
1. attribution is company-attributable or mixed, and
2. the account has experienced two or more separate incidents within a rolling sixty-day
window, and
3. the account has expressed, in writing or on a recorded call, an intention to review,
reduce or terminate the relationship,
a Relationship Recovery Allowance of up to USD 1,250 may be proposed. This is inclusive of,
not additional to, the uplifted cap under §7.3.
A Relationship Recovery Allowance requires joint approval by the Director of Customer
Experience and the Finance Director under §6, and must be accompanied by a written
recovery plan naming the root cause, the corrective action and the named relationship
owner. A payment without a plan is a discount, not a recovery, and is not authorised under
this policy.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §7.5] 7.5 Repeat-incident multiplier

Where the same customer experiences the same failure mode three or more times within
ninety days, the case must be escalated to the Director of Customer Experience irrespective
of value, and the underlying failure raised as a systemic issue. Repeat failures are a process
defect, and remedying them individually conceals the defect.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §8] 8 Cross-currency handling

Wholesale accounts are invoiced in their contracted currency. Caps in this document are
expressed in USD.
Conversion must be performed before comparison against a cap and before any
aggregation across accounts. A CAD amount compared directly against a USD cap will
systematically over-issue. Use the rate published for the incident date, not the rate on the
day the decision is taken, and record the rate used against the case.
Aggregate exposure reporting must convert every component to USD before summing.
Summing mixed-currency values and converting the total is not permitted and has
produced material misstatement in the past.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §9] 9 Communication standards

Remedy communications must:
• name the cause plainly, in the customer's language rather than internal terminology,
without disclosing supplier names, lot identifiers, batch numbers or commercial terms
• state what is being offered and what happens next, with a date
• avoid the passive voice when describing our own failures
• avoid offering an explanation the evidence does not support, including plausible-
sounding causes that have not been established
Where two independent causes affected the same customer, the communication must
address both. Merging two causes into a single tidier explanation is a misrepresentation,
and where one of the merged causes is company-attributable it also produces the wrong
remedy band.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §10] 10 Precedent log

Cases recorded for consistency. Precedent is persuasive, not binding.
PR-2024-03. Gold D2C subscriber, three consecutive deliveries arriving past promise
during a regional carrier dispute. Third-party-attributable. Standard gold cap applied at 120,
no uplift. Customer accepted. Upheld on review.
PR-2024-09. Standard wholesale account, espresso blend outside specification across a
two-week production window. Company-attributable. Uplifted to 500 under the then-draft
§7.3. Account retained. This case motivated the formal adoption of §7.3 in v4.0.
PR-2025-02. Flagship wholesale account, single late delivery caused by a port closure.
Third-party-attributable despite the account's insistence otherwise. Standard flagship cap
of 500 applied. Reviewed and upheld; external cause does not become internal because the
customer is important.
PR-2025-07. Bronze D2C customer, mis-picked order. Company-attributable, uplifted to 50.
Customer requested a larger credit citing inconvenience. Declined and upheld; tier and
attribution set the band, customer expectation does not.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §11] 11 Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | Jan 2021 | Initial issue |
| 2.0 | Jun 2022 | Wholesale tiers introduced |
| 3.0 | Nov 2023 | Approval matrix formalised; 150 threshold introduced |
| 3.1 | Mar 2024 | Caps revised upward; cross-currency rule added |
| 4.0 | Nov 2025 | §7 conditions and exceptions introduced; attribution categories defined; Relationship Recovery Allowance added; caps restated in §5 |

[MR-CC-POL-004 §Appendix A] Appendix A Quick reference, current caps

Standard, before uplift: bronze 25, silver 50, gold 120, trial 100, standard 250, flagship 500.
Human approval above 150 in all cases.
Company-attributable uplift: bronze 50, silver 120, gold 250, trial 250, standard 500, flagship 1,250.

[MR-CC-POL-004 §Appendix B] Appendix B Superseded caps, v3.1

Retained for audit of decisions taken between March 2024 and October 2025 only. These values are no longer in force and must not be applied to any case arising after 1 November 2025.

| Tier | v3.1 cap (USD) |
| :------------------ | :------------- |
| Bronze | 20 |
| Silver | 40 |
| Gold | 90 |
| Wholesale trial | 75 |
| Wholesale standard | 200 |
| Wholesale flagship | 350 |

Under v3.1 there was no attribution-based uplift and no Relationship Recovery Allowance. Cases arising before 1 November 2025 that were decided under those rules are not reopened.

[MR-QA-STD-002 §1] 1 Purpose

Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual
Meridian Roasters Co. Document reference: MR-QA-STD-002 Version: 2.3 Effective: 1
September 2025 Owner: Head of Quality Applies to: green coffee intake, lot release, blend
composition, roast production, finished-goods release Review cycle: annual

This manual defines the quality standards that green coffee must meet to be accepted, the
specifications each product must be built to, the conditions under which a component may
be substituted, and the records that must exist before finished goods are released for sale.
It is written for the quality team, the roasting team and production planning. Where it
conflicts with a production schedule, this manual takes precedence and the schedule
moves.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §2.1] 2.1 Method

All green coffee is evaluated on arrival using the SCA cupping protocol, ten cups per lot,
three assessors, scored independently before discussion. Scores are recorded to one
decimal place against the lot record.
Where assessors disagree by more than two points, a fourth assessor is brought in and the
lot is rescored. The original scores are retained; they are not overwritten.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §2.2] 2.2 Score bands

| Band | Score | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Exceptional | 88.0 and above | Single-origin release; micro-lot programme eligible |
| Speciality | 84.0 to 87.9 | Single-origin release; blend base eligible |
| Premium | 82.0 to 83.9 | Blend component only; not released as single origin |
| Commercial | 80.0 to 81.9 | Blend filler only, maximum thirty per cent of a blend by weight |
| Reject | Below 80.0 | Not released. Quarantine and supplier claim under MR-PROC-HB-003 §7 |
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §2.3] 2.3 Score is a property of the lot, not the supplier

A supplier who consistently delivers at 86 has not thereby earned an 86 on an unscored lot.
Every lot is scored on arrival. No lot enters production on the basis of the supplier's history.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual
chunks.section_title: Score is a property of the lot, not the supplier

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §3] 3 Product specifications

Each product has a written specification. Production against a specification that has not been met is a deviation and is handled under §5.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §3.1] 3.1 Cascadia Blend (SKU MR-BLD-001)

The company's highest-volume product and the base of most subscription plans.
| Attribute | Specification |
| :---------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| Base component | Colombian washed, 60% by weight |
| Secondary component | Guatemalan washed, 25% by weight |
| Balance | Brazilian natural, 15% by weight |
| Minimum cupping score, base component | 84.0 |
| Minimum cupping score, secondary | 83.0 |
| Minimum cupping score, balance | 80.0 |
| Roast profile | Medium, first crack plus 1:45 to 2:10 |
| Target finished cup | Balanced, sweet, cocoa and stone fruit, medium acidity |
The Colombian base is what customers recognise as Cascadia. It carries the sweetness and the acidity structure. Substituting the base changes the character of the cup more than any other single change available to us, and subscription customers who have drunk it for months will notice within one bag.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §3.2] 3.2 Other products

| SKU | Product | Base origin | Min base score |
| :---------- | :---------------- | :------------------------ | :------------- |
| MR-BLD-002 | Nightwatch Blend | Sumatra | 82.0 |
| MR-BLD-003 | Harbour Espresso | Brazilian natural | 82.0 |
| MR-SO-011 | Yirgacheffe Kochere | Ethiopian washed | 86.0 |
| MR-SO-012 | Huila Reserva | Colombian washed | 86.0 |
| MR-SO-013 | Sumatra Lintong | Sumatra wet-hulled | 84.0 |
| MR-SO-014 | Cerrado Amarelo | Brazilian natural | 84.0 |
| MR-DEC-001 | Quietwater Decaf | Colombian, EA process | 83.0 |
Single-origin products may not be substituted at all. If the named origin is unavailable, the product goes out of stock. This is not negotiable and has been tested twice.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §4] 4 Lot release

A green lot may enter production only when all of the following exist on the lot record:
* a cupping score from three assessors
* a moisture reading between 10.0 and 12.0 per cent
* a defect count within grade
* an intake date and a linked purchase order
* no open supplier claim against the lot
A lot that has been in the silo more than nine months from intake must be re-cupped before use. Green coffee ages. A lot that scored 84 on arrival may not score 84 a year later, and an aged lot used at its original score is a specification failure hiding behind a stale record.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5] 5 Substitution policy

This is the most consequential section in this manual and the one most often applied under time pressure.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5.1] 5.1 When substitution may be considered

Substitution of a blend component may be considered only when:
* the specified component is genuinely unavailable, not merely inconvenient to retrieve, and
* the alternative component meets the minimum score for the position it is filling, and
* the substitution is recorded on the batch record before the roast, not after
Production pressure is not a justification. Running out of a product is an acceptable outcome and is always preferable to shipping something the customer did not order under a name they recognise.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5.2] 5.2 Authority

| Substitution | Authority |
|---|---|
| Within the same origin, score delta 1.0 or less | Roast lead |
| Cross-origin, score delta 2.0 or less | QA Lead |
| Cross-origin, score delta above 2.0 | QA Lead and Head of Quality, jointly |
| Any substitution affecting a blend's named base component | Head of Quality, in writing |
| Any substitution on a single-origin product | Not permitted under any authority |
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5.3] 5.3 Score delta

Score delta is the difference between the cupping score of the specified component and the
cupping score of the substitute. It is calculated against the specification minimum, not
against the score of the lot that happened to be in use last week.
Example. Cascadia Blend base carries a specification minimum of 84.0. A substitute lot
scoring 79.5 gives a delta of 4.5, which is above the 2.0 threshold, requires joint QA Lead and
Head of Quality authority under §5.2, and triggers the notification obligation in §5.4.
A substitute scoring below 80.0 is in the Reject band under §2.2 and may not be used in any
blend regardless of authority. A substitute between 80.0 and 81.9 is Commercial band and
may not exceed thirty per cent of the blend by weight, which disqualifies it from any base
position.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5.4] 5.4 Customer notification obligation

Where a substitution produces a score delta greater than 2.0 points against
specification, affected customers must be notified before or with despatch.
The notification must:
• state that the product differs from its usual composition
• state the nature of the difference in plain terms
• offer the customer the option to decline the shipment or to substitute a different
product at no charge
• be issued to every customer whose order contains the affected batch, including
wholesale accounts
The obligation sits with the Head of Quality to raise and with Customer Experience to
execute. It is not discretionary and it is not waived by a judgement that the cup is "probably
fine". A customer who discovers the substitution by tasting it has been denied a choice they
were entitled to make.
Failure to notify where notification was required is a quality incident in its own right,
independent of whether any customer complains, and must be raised as such.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §5.5] 5.5 Batch record requirements

Every substitution must be recorded on the batch record with:
• the specified component and the substitute used
• both cupping scores and the calculated delta
• the authorising individual and the authority level applied
• whether notification was required under §5.4, and if so, the date it issued
• the reason the specified component was unavailable
A QA note on the batch record that describes a substitution but does not record the authority, the delta and the notification status is incomplete and is a finding in its own right at audit.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §6] 6 QA note taxonomy

Batch records carry free-text QA notes. Notes are classified as follows and should be written so the class is unambiguous.
| Class | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Observation | A characteristic worth recording, no deviation | None |
| Deviation | Production departed from specification | Root cause required within five working days |
| Concession | A deviation accepted under named authority | Authority must be recorded |
| Hold | Batch not released pending investigation | Blocks despatch |
A note describing a substitution and a flatter cup profile is a deviation, and if the batch was released it is a concession, which means an authority must be recorded against it. A batch released with a deviation note and no recorded authority is a control failure whether or not the coffee was acceptable.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §7] 7 Finished-goods release

Finished goods are released when:
* the batch record is complete, including any substitution record under §5.5
* a post-roast cup has been taken and scored against the product's target profile
* any notification obligation under §5.4 has been discharged, or explicitly recorded as not applicable with a reason
Release is a positive act. A batch that nobody blocked has not been released; it has been overlooked.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §8] 8 Roast profile control

Each product has a target profile expressed as time from first crack. Profiles are held in the roasting system and are not adjusted to compensate for green quality. Roasting a flatter lot darker to mask the difference is expressly prohibited: it changes the product the customer receives while concealing the reason, and it defeats the notification obligation in §5.4 by removing the evidence a cupper would use.
Where a substitute component genuinely requires a different approach, that is a new
product specification and goes through §3, not through an undocumented profile
adjustment on the day.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §9] 9 Traceability

Every finished bag must be traceable to its roast batch, every roast batch to its green lot,
every green lot to its purchase order, and every purchase order to its supplier. The chain is:
order line -> roast batch -> green lot -> purchase order -> supplier

This chain exists so that a quality complaint can be resolved against evidence rather than
against opinion. Where the chain is broken at any hop, the complaint cannot be attributed,
and under MR-CC-POL-004 §7.1 an unattributable quality complaint is treated as
company-attributable.

Traceability records are retained for three years.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:
[MR-QA-STD-002 §10] 10 Known risks

Recorded here because they have materialised before.

Single-origin dependency on the Colombian base. Cascadia Blend's base component has
one qualified supplier. Any interruption to that supply forces a choice between a
substitution above the §5.3 threshold and a stock-out. There is no third option, and
pretending otherwise under pressure is how §5.4 gets missed. Qualification of a second
Colombian source has been on the procurement plan since 2024.

Aged balance-component lots. Brazilian natural lots held for the balance position tend to
sit longest in the silo and are the most likely to be reached for in a shortage. They are also
the most likely to have aged past their recorded score. See §4 on re-cupping at nine months.

Substitution under despatch pressure. Substitution decisions are made on production
mornings when a roast is scheduled and the silo is short. That is precisely when the
authority requirements in §5.2 and the notification obligation in §5.4 are most likely to be
skipped, because both require someone outside the roastery to be available.
chunks.doc_title: Green Coffee Quality Standards & Roasting QA Manual

chunks.text:

| Version | Date | Change |

| 2.1 | Nov 2023 | Nine-month re-cupping requirement added |

chunks.text:
[MR-PROC-HB-003 §1] 1 Purpose

Supplier Agreements & Procurement Handbook
Meridian Roasters Co. Document reference: MR-PROC-HB-003 Version: 3.0 Effective: 1
July 2025 Owner: Head of Procurement Classification: Internal — commercial terms, not for
customer disclosure Review cycle: annual, and on execution of any new supply agreement

This handbook summarises the commercial terms Meridian Roasters holds with each
green coffee supplier, explains how performance against those terms is measured, and
defines the process by which a supplier relationship is reviewed, remediated or ended.
Contract summaries in §3 are abstracts. The executed agreements are held by Legal and
prevail in any dispute. Where a summary here and an executed contract differ, the contract
governs and this handbook is wrong and must be corrected.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §2] 2 How we buy

Meridian buys green coffee on fixed-price forward contracts, denominated in USD, on FOB
terms from origin port. We take title at the origin port rail and carry the freight, insurance
and arrival risk from that point.
This matters for how delay is treated. Because we are the party arranging carriage from
FOB, an ocean delay after loading is ordinarily our risk, not the supplier's. The exceptions
are set out in §4.3 and are the subject of specific negotiated carve-outs with two of our five
suppliers.
Purchase orders are raised against an annual volume commitment with quarterly call-offs.
Lead time runs from purchase order date to arrival at the Port of Portland, and is the
measure used throughout this handbook.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §3.1] 3.1 Finca La Esperanza — Colombia (SUP-01)

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| Relationship since | April 2019 |
| Origin region | Huila |
| Load port | Cartagena |
| Incoterm | FOB Cartagena |
| Currency | USD |
| Contracted lead time | 42 days, purchase order to Portland arrival |
| Tolerance | ± 7 days |
| Annual volume commitment | 36,000 kg |
| Quality floor | Cupping 84.0, Grade 1 |
| Notice period | 120 days |
| Force majeure | §9.1 applies with the carve-out at §9.2 |

Strategic note. Finca La Esperanza is our sole qualified source for the Colombian washed base of Cascadia Blend, our highest-volume product. There is no second qualified Colombian source. Qualification of an alternate has been on the procurement plan since Q3 2024 and has not been completed. Until it is, every delay at this supplier propagates directly into product quality under MR-QA-STD-002 §10, and the sole-source review trigger at §11.1 applies rather than the standard trigger at §11.2.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §4.1] 4.1 The three figures, and which one is meant

Three different numbers are routinely called "lead time" inside Meridian. They are not interchangeable and confusing them is the single most common analytical error in procurement reporting.
**Contracted target.** The figure in the agreement, held on the supplier record. A property of the contract, not of any shipment.
**Actual lead time.** Days elapsed from purchase order date to actual arrival at Portland. A property of a specific purchase order. Where the phrase "lead time" is used without qualification in this handbook, in reporting, or in conversation, it means this figure.
**Estimated arrival.** The carrier's ETA at time of booking. Useful for planning, useless for performance measurement, and never the basis of a breach assessment.
chunks.section_title: The three figures, and which one is meant

chunks.text:
[MR-PROC-HB-003 §4.2] 4.2 Variance and breach

Variance is actual lead time minus contracted target.
A purchase order is **within tolerance** where variance falls inside the tolerance band in §3. A purchase order is **in breach** where variance exceeds the tolerance band, unless relieved under §9.
Variance is assessed per purchase order. A supplier's average variance across a year can sit
comfortably inside tolerance while individual orders breach badly, and it is individual
breaches that damage production. Average variance is a relationship health indicator;
individual breach count is the contractual measure. Reporting that shows only the average
will conceal exactly the events this handbook exists to manage.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §4.3] 4.3 Worked example

A purchase order raised on a supplier with a 42-day contracted target and ±7 tolerance,
arriving 68 days after the purchase order date, has an actual lead time of 68 days and a
variance of +26 days. This exceeds the tolerance band by 19 days and is a breach unless
relieved under §9.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §5] 5 Quality claims

Where a delivered lot scores below the contractual quality floor, a claim is raised within
fourteen days of cupping. Remedies available, in order of preference:

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §3] 3 Rejection and full credit

A lot in the Reject band under MR-QA-STD-002 §2.2 is rejected outright and is not
negotiated down into a blend.
Claims are tracked against the supplier record and count toward the review triggers in §11.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §6] 6 Payment and currency

Payment terms are net 30 from bill of lading date, in USD, against documents. FX exposure
sits between contract price in USD and revenue in USD, CAD, GBP and EUR, and is reported
monthly by Finance.
Procurement does not hedge. Where a currency movement materially changes landed cost,
that is reported rather than managed at the purchase order level.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §7] 7 Supplier quality claims and counterclaims

Suppliers may claim against Meridian for wrongful rejection, late payment, or failure to
take contracted volume. Counterclaims are handled by Legal and are recorded on the
supplier record so that any review under §11 sees both directions of the relationship. A
supplier with three breaches against us and two legitimate counterclaims against them is a
different conversation from one with three breaches and a clean record.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §8] 8 Ordering and call-off discipline

Quarterly call-offs must be raised at least one full lead time plus tolerance before the
required arrival date. A purchase order raised late produces a late arrival that is not a
supplier breach, and misclassifying our own planning failure as a supplier breach corrupts
the review process at §11.
Where a call-off is raised late, the purchase order record must be annotated accordingly. An
unannotated late arrival is assessed as a supplier breach by default.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §9.1] 9.1 Standard clause

A supplier is relieved of lead-time obligations where performance is prevented by an event
beyond their reasonable control, including natural disaster, civil unrest, government action,
crop failure attributable to extreme weather, and labour action at origin not involving the
supplier's own workforce.

Relief requires written notice within five business days of the supplier becoming aware of
the event, and requires the supplier to demonstrate that the event actually prevented
performance rather than merely made it more difficult.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §9.2] 9.2 Carve-out — port congestion and vessel scheduling

Applies to Finca La Esperanza (SUP-01) and Lintong Highlands (SUP-04) only.
The following are expressly excluded from force majeure relief under these two
agreements:
* port congestion at the load port
* vessel roll-over, missed sailings and carrier scheduling failures
* container availability and equipment shortage
* delays in export documentation or customs clearance at origin

The commercial rationale is that these events are foreseeable at both ports, are within the
supplier's capacity to manage through earlier booking and alternate carrier arrangements,
and have materialised repeatedly. The supplier is expected to book with sufficient margin
that ordinary congestion does not breach the contracted lead time.

A delay caused by port congestion or a missed sailing at Cartagena or Belawan is therefore
a breach, not a relieved event, and counts toward the review triggers in §11.

Suppliers under §9.2 were compensated for accepting the carve-out through a price
adjustment at the relevant renewal. It is a paid-for term, not an imposition, and should be
enforced accordingly.
chunks.section_title: Carve-out — port congestion and vessel scheduling

chunks.text:
[MR-PROC-HB-003 §9.3] 9.3 Relief does not cancel the operational consequence

A supplier properly relieved under §9.1 still leaves Meridian without coffee. Force majeure
governs contractual liability, not production planning. A relieved delay must still be raised
operationally so that quality and production can plan a response under MR-QA-STD-002
§5, and so that the customer-facing consequence is attributed correctly under MR-CC-POL-
004 §7.1.

The attribution question and the liability question are separate. A supply failure that is
contractually the supplier's fault may still be company-attributable for customer remedy
purposes, because from the customer's point of view we shipped a product that did not
meet its specification.
chunks.section_title: Relief does not cancel the operational consequence

chunks.text:
[MR-PROC-HB-003 §10] 10 Remedy ladder for supplier breach

| Step | Trigger | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | First breach in rolling 12 months | Written notice, recorded on supplier record |
| 2 | Second breach | Formal performance conversation, corrective action plan requested |
| 3 | Third breach, or second at a sole- source supplier | Supplier review under §11 |
| 4 | Review outcome | Remediation plan, volume reduction, or notice to terminate |

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §11.1] 11.1 Sole-source suppliers

Where a supplier is the only qualified source for a component, review is triggered by two
breaches within a rolling twelve months, rather than three. The lower threshold reflects
that a sole-source failure has no mitigation and propagates directly into product.
Review of a sole-source supplier must consider, and record, the following before any
recommendation is made:
*   breach history with variance for each breach
*   whether any breach was relieved under §9, and if so on what evidence
*   downstream quality impact, including any substitution made under MR-QA-STD-002
    §5 as a consequence
*   customer impact and remedy cost arising
*   the state of alternate source qualification
*   the practical consequence of termination given no alternate exists
A recommendation to terminate a sole-source supplier without a qualified alternate in place
is a recommendation to discontinue the affected product. That is a commercial decision for
the Commercial Director and the Managing Director jointly, not a procurement decision,
and it must be presented as the product decision it actually is.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §11.2] 11.2 Multi-source suppliers

Three breaches within a rolling twelve months, or two quality claims, or any single breach
exceeding thirty days' variance.

[MR-PROC-HB-003 §11.3] 11.3 What a review cannot settle

A supplier review assembles evidence. It does not, by itself, answer whether a relationship
should end. That question weighs contractual performance against switching cost,
qualification lead time, relationship history, origin availability and product strategy, and
several of those inputs are judgements held outside procurement.
Reviews that present a termination recommendation as though it followed arithmetically
from the breach count have overstepped, and are returned.

[MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE §INC-2024-03] INC-2024-03 Carrier sortation failure, Pacific Northwest

Incident Post-Mortem Archive
Meridian Roasters Co. Document reference: MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE Maintained by:
Operations Coverage: 2024 — present Classification: Internal

How to read this archive
Every incident above severity 3 gets a post-mortem within ten working days. The format is
fixed: summary, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, customer impact, what we did,
and action items with an owner and a status.
Action item status is the most important field in this document. An open action item
from eighteen months ago is not history, it is a live risk, and it is the reason most repeat
incidents repeat.

Severity scale:
| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Single customer, contained, no systemic signal |
| 2 | Multiple customers, one product or one route, resolved within a week |
| 3 | Multiple customers across a product line, or any incident with a quality-specification deviation |
| 4 | Material revenue or relationship risk, or a control failure |
| 5 | Regulatory, safety, or existential |

Severity: 2 Opened: 11 March 2024 Closed: 22 March 2024 Owner: Fulfilment Operations

Summary
Approximately 90 parcels routed through a carrier sortation hub in Tacoma were held for
six to nine days following a facility systems failure at the carrier. Customers in Washington
and Oregon were affected.

Timeline
* 9 Mar — Carrier facility systems failure, not notified to shippers
* 11 Mar — First customer contacts received; tracking showing no movement
* 12 Mar — Carrier confirms facility issue on escalation
* 14 Mar — Affected parcel list assembled; proactive notification issued
* 18 Mar — Parcels begin moving
* 22 Mar — Last parcel delivered
Root cause
External. Carrier facility failure with no shipper notification.
Contributing factors
We learned of the problem from customers rather than from the carrier or from our own
monitoring. Nothing in our systems watched for parcels whose tracking had stopped
updating.
Customer impact
90 parcels, 71 customers. 38 tickets raised. Remedies issued under the third-party-
attributable band, total USD 1,840.
Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stalled-tracking alert where a parcel shows no scan for 72 hours | Fulfilment | Closed Jun 2024 |
| 2 | Carrier notification SLA written into the next contract renewal | Procurement | Closed Nov 2024 |
Note
This incident is the reason we have stalled-tracking alerting at all. It worked as designed in
February 2026.

[MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE §INC-2024-11] INC-2024-11 Belawan port closure and Nightwatch substitution

Severity: 4 Opened: 6 November 2024 Closed: 3 December 2024 Owner: Head of Quality
Summary
A port closure at Belawan delayed the Sumatran green coffee that forms the base of
Nightwatch Blend by 23 days. With no Sumatran green in the silo and a scheduled roast,
production substituted a Guatemalan lot into the base position of Nightwatch Blend across
eleven roast batches between 12 and 27 November.
The substitute lot scored 81.2 against a Nightwatch base specification minimum of 82.0, a
delta of 0.8 against specification — but the lot previously in use had scored 85.1, so the delta
as customers experienced it was 3.9 points. The resulting cup was materially different: less
body, more acidity, none of the earthy character Nightwatch drinkers buy it for.
No customer notification was issued. Quality complaints began arriving on 25 November,
roughly two weeks after the first affected batches shipped, and continued into mid-
December.
Timeline
• 14 Oct — Belawan port closure begins
• 18 Oct — Supplier notifies delay; relief claimed under force majeure
• 12 Nov — First substituted roast batch produced. QA note recorded. Substitution
authorised verbally by the roast lead
• 27 Nov — Colombian-sourced Sumatran replacement arrives; substitution ends
• 25 Nov — First quality complaint received
• 2 Dec — Complaint volume recognised as a cluster rather than noise
• 3 Dec — Root cause established by tracing complaints to batch records
Root cause
A blend base component was substituted with a materially lower-scoring lot, and
customers were not told.
Contributing factors
Five, and all five are the reason this post-mortem matters.
No notification obligation existed. The QA manual at v2.2 did not require customer
notification for any substitution. The decision to notify was discretionary and nobody made
it.
Authority was inadequate. The substitution was authorised verbally by the roast lead. The
manual at the time permitted this. A base-component substitution on a flagship blend was
being decided by the person under the most schedule pressure.
Score delta was calculated against the wrong baseline. The team compared the substitute
against the specification minimum (0.8, felt tolerable) rather than against the lot actually in
use (3.9, obviously not tolerable). Customers do not taste the specification. They taste last
month's bag.
The complaint cluster took seven days to recognise. Individual agents saw individual
complaints. Nobody was looking at complaint rate by product against a baseline.
The connection to the port closure was never made until day 27. Procurement knew
about the delay in October. Customer care saw complaints in late November. The two facts
sat in different systems owned by different teams and nobody joined them, because no
single role had reason to look at both.
Customer impact
Approximately 340 D2C customers and 2 wholesale accounts received affected product. 61
quality tickets. 14 subscription cancellations in the following eight weeks, against a baseline
of 3 to 5. One wholesale account, since retained, went to formal review of the supply
relationship.
Remedy cost USD 4,120, issued under the then-current v3.1 caps with no attribution uplift
available. Several customers were, in hindsight, under- remedied for what was a company-
attributable failure — which is the finding that eventually produced §7.3 of the remedy
policy.

What we did
Substitution ended when replacement green arrived. Affected customers were contacted
retrospectively with an explanation and a credit. The wholesale account was visited in
person.

Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add a customer notification obligation for substitutions above a defined score delta, to the QA manual | Head of Quality | Closed Sep 2025 — issued as MR-QA-STD-002 v2.3 §5.4 |
| 2 | Raise substitution authority for base components to Head of Quality, in writing | Head of Quality | Closed Sep 2025 — §5.2 |
| 3 | Implement an automated customer notification trigger on any blend substitution exceeding 2.0 cupping points, firing at batch release rather than relying on a manual step | Engineering | OPEN — not implemented. Deferred Q1 2025, deferred again Q3 2025, carried into the 2026 plan. Currently unscheduled. |
| 4 | Complaint-rate monitoring by product against a rolling baseline, alerting on deviation | CX Analytics | OPEN — partially implemented. Reporting exists; alerting does not. A cluster is still recognised by a human noticing. |
| 5 | Negotiate a port-congestion carve-out from force majeure at the next Lintong renewal | Procurement | Closed Jul 2025 — MR-PROC-HB-003 §9.2 |
| 6 | Sole-source review trigger lowered to two breaches | Procurement | Closed Sep 2024 — §11.1 |
| 7 | Qualify a second source for every sole-sourced blend base component | Procurement | OPEN. Sumatran alternate qualified Mar 2025. Colombian alternate not qualified. Carried since Q3 2024. |
Standing lesson
This incident had a supply cause, a quality consequence and a customer consequence, and each was visible to a different team. None of the three teams could see the whole shape of it. The delay was known twenty-seven days before the first complaint was understood.
The controls that would have caught it — an automated notification trigger and complaint-rate alerting — are action items 3 and 4, and both remain open.

[MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE §INC-2025-04] INC-2025-04 Decaf mislabelling

Severity: 3 Opened: 18 April 2025 Closed: 29 April 2025 Owner: Production
Summary
A packaging run applied Quietwater Decaf labels to approximately 200 bags of regular Cascadia Blend following a label reel change on the wrong line.
Root cause
Human error at line changeover, with no verification step between label load and run start.
Customer impact
47 customers received caffeinated coffee labelled as decaf. This is a consumer safety matter, not merely a quality one. All affected customers were contacted within 24 hours of discovery with an explicit instruction not to consume, and a full refund plus replacement was issued regardless of tier.
Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Barcode verification at label load, blocking run start on mismatch | Production | Closed Jul 2025 |
| 2 | Decaf runs physically segregated to a dedicated line | Production | Closed Jun 2025 |

Note
The remedy here was issued without reference to caps, correctly. Safety overrides the remedy ladder. MR-CC-POL-004 §1 carries this forward.

[MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE §INC-2025-09] INC-2025-09 Subscription billing duplication

Severity: 3 Opened: 2 September 2025 Closed: 9 September 2025 Owner: Engineering
Summary
A retry loop in the subscription billing job double-charged 118 subscribers on the 1 September cycle.
Root cause
A payment gateway timeout was treated as a failure rather than an unknown, and the job
retried a charge that had in fact succeeded.
Customer impact
118 customers. All duplicates refunded within 72 hours. 34 tickets. No cancellations
attributable.

| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Idempotency keys on all charge operations | Engineering | Closed Sep 2025 |
| 2 | Timeouts treated as indeterminate, requiring reconciliation before retry | Engineering | Closed Oct 2025 |

[MR-OPS-PM-ARCHIVE §INC-2025-12] INC-2025-12 Wholesale delivery window misses, Toronto

Severity: 2 Opened: 14 December 2025 Closed: 20 December 2025 Owner: Fulfilment
Operations
Summary
Four consecutive wholesale deliveries to Toronto accounts arrived outside the agreed
morning delivery window during the December peak, disrupting café opening preparation.
Root cause
Peak-season carrier capacity. Our wholesale deliveries were consolidated into a standard
service rather than the committed window service, to manage cost.
Contributing factors
The decision to consolidate was taken in fulfilment without reference to the wholesale
delivery commitments in the account agreements. Nobody checked what we had promised.
Customer impact
Three accounts, including Rosewood Coffee House, which raised it directly with its account
manager and asked whether the committed window was contractual. It is.
Action items
| # | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wholesale delivery commitments surfaced in the fulfilment planning view | Fulfilment | Closed Feb 2026 |
| 2 | Peak-season capacity booked in advance for committed-window accounts | Fulfilment | OPEN. Scheduled for the 2026 peak planning cycle, not yet done. |

Note
Rosewood Coffee House. Worth reading alongside anything else concerning that account, because this sits inside the rolling window that matters for relationship history.

Open action items, consolidated
Current as of the last archive review.

| Ref | Action | Owner | Age |
|---|---|---|---|
| INC-2024-11 #3 | Automated substitution notification trigger | Engineering | 15 months |
| INC-2024-11 #4 | Complaint-rate alerting by product | CX Analytics | 15 months |
| INC-2024-11 #7 | Colombian alternate source qualification | Procurement | 15 months |
